sections.title: Architecture Overview
sections.content:
## 2. Architecture Overview

### Solution Summary
The Guardrail Damage Detection System is an automated, AWS-based computer vision architecture designed to replace labor-intensive manual reviews of long-form GoPro inspection footage. Authorized county users authenticate via Amazon Cognito federated to county Active Directory (AD FS) and upload raw inspection videos directly to Amazon S3 via presigned multipart uploads (FR-001). An Amazon EventBridge rule triggers an AWS Step Functions workflow that orchestrates GPMF telemetry extraction via AWS Fargate, video segmentation via AWS Elemental MediaConvert, and distance-based frame extraction every 3 meters (FR-002, FR-003).

Extracted frames undergo quality gating via an FFmpeg blurdetect filter on AWS Fargate before being processed through a Detection Service adapter layer calling Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels object detection (FR-004, FR-005). Step Functions explicitly manages the lifecycle of the inference endpoint to control costs (AC-008). Raw bounding-box detections are clustered and consolidated by GPS proximity, time, and category into a deduplicated review queue stored in Amazon DynamoDB (FR-006). County reviewers utilize a React-based review application to approve, dismiss, or recategorize findings, maintaining a fully audited decision trail (FR-007). Finally, confirmed damage data is surfaced through an integrated Esri ArcGIS map dashboard and exported via multi-format reporting tools (FR-008).

### Architecture Style
Serverless & Event-Driven — Selected because the ingestion workload is sporadic (per inspection drive), requiring elastic compute scaling without idle infrastructure costs. AWS Step Functions, Amazon S3, Amazon EventBridge, and AWS Fargate provide a fully managed, decoupled pipeline capable of handling large binary files (1-2 hour videos) and parallelizing frame extraction via distributed mapping without hitting single-function execution limits (NFR-Scalability).

### Key Architectural Decisions
| Decision | Rationale | Requirement Trace |
|----------|-----------|------------------|
| Direct-to-S3 Presigned Multipart Uploads | Bypasses API Gateway and Lambda payload limits when ingesting large 1-2 hour GoPro video files. | FR-001, AC-002 |
| AWS Step Functions & AWS Fargate Pipeline | Orchestrates long-running video processing, telemetry extraction, and distance-based frame sampling without execution timeout limits. | FR-003, NFR-Scalability |
| Pre-transcoding GPMF Telemetry Extraction | Extracts the complete GPMF stream from unmodified video files on Fargate to protect frame-to-location correlation accuracy. | FR-002, AC-004 |
| Explicit Rekognition Endpoint Start/Stop in Step Functions | Controls operational expenditure by ensuring the Custom Labels inference endpoint is active only during active processing stages. | AC-008, R-003 |
| Amazon DynamoDB for Review Queue and Audit Trail | Provides low-latency storage for deduplicated review items, point-in-time recovery, and immutable audit logs of human review decisions. | FR-006, FR-007, NFR-Availability |
| Amazon Cognito Federated to AD FS | Satisfies county security mandates by leveraging existing Active Directory credentials without maintaining a separate user store. | FR-001, NFR-Security, AC-001 |
| Esri ArcGIS Integration | Connects confirmed findings directly to the county's existing GIS mapping and reporting stack via shared query logic. | FR-008, AC-011, AC-012 |

## 3. System Context

### External Systems & Integrations
| System | Purpose | Direction | Protocol |
|--------|---------|-----------|----------|
| County Active Directory (AD FS) | User authentication and identity federation via Amazon Cognito | Inbound | SAML 2.0 / OIDC [Source: REQ-001, FR-001, AC-001] |
| Esri ArcGIS Platform | Map dashboard visualization and geospatial reporting of confirmed guardrail damage findings | Outbound | REST API / GeoJSON [Source: REQ-001, FR-008, AC-011] |

### Users & Actors
| Actor | Role | Interaction |
|-------|------|-------------|
| County Inspector / User | Authenticated county staff | Logs into the React web application via Cognito/AD FS, uploads long-form GoPro video files, reviews and processes flagged defect items in the review queue, and accesses map dashboards/reports [Source: REQ-001, FR-001, FR-007, FR-008] |

### System Boundaries
**Inside the system:**
- React Upload and Reviewer Web Applications (Frontend UI hosting user upload and defect review queues) [Source: REQ-001, FR-001, FR-007]
- Amazon Cognito (User authentication and AD FS federation) [Source: REQ-001, FR-001, AC-001]
- Amazon S3 Raw Landing Zone & Processed Buckets (Storage for raw GoPro video files, normalized GPS tracks, and geotagged frames) [Source: REQ-001, FR-001, FR-002, FR-003]
- Amazon EventBridge & AWS Step Functions (Event routing and automated processing pipeline orchestration) [Source: REQ-001, FR-003]
- AWS Elemental MediaConvert (Video segmentation and transcoding) [Source: REQ-001, FR-003]
- AWS Fargate Compute Environment (Telemetry extraction, distance-based frame sampling, and FFmpeg blur filtering tasks) [Source: REQ-001, FR-002, FR-003, FR-004]
- Detection Service Adapter Layer & Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels (Object detection model inference for guardrail defects with automated endpoint start/stop lifecycle management) [Source: REQ-001, FR-005, AC-008]
- Detection Clustering and Consolidation Engine (GPS/time proximity deduplication of raw bounding-box detections) [Source: REQ-001, FR-006]
- Amazon DynamoDB (Storage for consolidated review items, review audit trails, and future model retraining datasets) [Source: REQ-001, FR-007, Data Requirements]

**Outside the system (external dependencies):**
- County Active Directory (AD FS) [Source: REQ-001, FR-001, AC-001]
- Esri ArcGIS Platform (County GIS stack) [Source: REQ-001, FR-008, AC-011]
- GoPro Field Vehicles & Inspection Cameras (Source of raw video footage and embedded GPMF telemetry) [Source: REQ-001, Current Process, Data Sources]

## 4. Component Architecture

### Component Overview
| Component | Responsibility | Type | Requirement Trace |
|-----------|---------------|------|------------------|
| React Upload Application | Provides a secure web interface for authorized county users to authenticate via Cognito and upload long-form GoPro videos using presigned multipart uploads. | Service (Frontend) | FR-001, AC-001, AC-002 |
| React Reviewer Application | Provides a web interface for reviewing flagged guardrail defects with bounding-box overlays, managing review queues, recording decisions, and displaying inspection data. | Service (Frontend) | FR-007, AC-010 |
| Amazon Cognito | Manages user authentication and federates access to the county's Active Directory via AD FS (Active Directory Federation Services). | Service (Managed Cloud) | FR-001, 7.2 Security, AC-001 |
| Amazon S3 Raw Video Bucket | Stores incoming, uncompressed long-form GoPro video files with standard S3 access controls, versioning, and lifecycle policies. | Service (Storage) | FR-001, 7.3 Availability, 8. Data Retention, AC-002 |
| Amazon EventBridge | Detects S3 object-created events from the raw-video bucket and explicitly/filterably routes them to initiate the Step Functions pipeline. | Service (Integration) | FR-003, AC-003 |
| AWS Step Functions Pipeline | Orchestrates the end-to-end processing workflow, including lifecycle management of the inference endpoint, video segmentation, distributed map task dispatch, and error routing. | Service (Orchestration) | FR-003, FR-005, 7.4 Scalability, AC-003, AC-005, AC-008 |
| AWS Elemental MediaConvert | Segments and transcodes long-form video files into manageable chunks following GPS telemetry extraction. | Service (Media Processing) | FR-003, AC-005 |
| AWS Fargate Telemetry Extraction Service | Decodes the complete GPMF telemetry stream from original video files prior to transcoding to generate a normalized GPS track (JSON/Parquet) written to S3. | Service (Compute Container) | FR-002, 8. Data Sources, AC-004 |
| AWS Fargate Frame Processing Service | Executes distributed map tasks to sample video frames at distance intervals (every 3 meters), applies FFmpeg blur detection filtering, and correlates frames with GPS tracks. | Service (Compute Container) | FR-003, FR-004, AC-005, AC-006 |
| Detection Service Adapter Layer | Interfaces between processing tasks and the underlying computer vision model, submitting usable frames and receiving bounding boxes and categories. | Service (Application Logic) | FR-005, AC-007 |
| Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels | Performs object detection on filtered video frames to identify specified guardrail defect categories and return bounding boxes, categories, and confidence scores. | Service (AI/ML Managed) | FR-005, 9. AI Requirements, AC-007 |
| Detection Consolidation & Clustering Service | Clusters raw bounding-box detections across multiple frames using GPS proximity, time, and category into a single deduplicated review item. | Service (Application Logic) | FR-006, AC-009 |
| Amazon DynamoDB | Stores consolidated defect items, review decisions, immutable audit trails, and review-labeled datasets, configured with point-in-time recovery. | Service (Database) | FR-007, 7.3 Availability, 8. Data Retention, AC-010 |
| Esri ArcGIS Integration Service | Integrates confirmed damage findings and shared query logic with the county's existing Esri ArcGIS platform to support map dashboards and report generation. | Service (GIS Integration) | FR-008, AC-011, AC-012 |

### Component Interactions
- **Client-to-Storage (Synchronous/HTTPS):** Authenticated county users interact via the React Upload Application to request presigned multipart upload URLs from an API Gateway / AWS Lambda backend (DEFAULT — not specified in requirements), then upload GoPro video binaries directly to the Amazon S3 Raw Video Bucket via HTTPS.
- **Event-Driven Orchestration (Asynchronous):** Object creation events in Amazon S3 are captured by Amazon EventBridge, which triggers the AWS Step Functions workflow asynchronously.
- **Processing Pipeline Execution (Synchronous & Asynchronous):** The Step Functions workflow sequentially invokes AWS Fargate Telemetry Extraction Service to parse GPMF streams, initiates AWS Elemental MediaConvert for video chunking, and deploys Distributed Map tasks to fan out parallel AWS Fargate Frame Processing tasks.
- **AI Inference & Lifecycle Control (Synchronous):** Step Functions explicitly issues API calls to start the Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels endpoint, streams filtered frames through the Detection Service Adapter Layer, retrieves object detection payloads, and explicitly stops the endpoint.
- **Persistence & Review (Asynchronous/Synchronous):** The Consolidation Service writes deduplicated records to Amazon DynamoDB. Reviewers interact with the React Reviewer Application to read/write review decisions and audit trails directly against DynamoDB.
- **GIS & Reporting Export (Synchronous):** The Esri ArcGIS Integration Service and reporting modules query DynamoDB using shared query logic to render map layers and export CSV, PDF, and GeoJSON reports.

### Component Details

#### React Upload Application
- **Responsibility:** Provide a secure user interface for authenticated county users to upload long-form GoPro video files containing embedded GPMF telemetry.
- **Interfaces:** HTTPS web interface exposed to users; direct presigned S3 upload endpoints.
- **Dependencies:** Amazon Cognito, Amazon S3 Raw Video Bucket.
- **Technology:** React (TypeScript) hosted on Amazon S3 / Amazon CloudFront (DEFAULT — not specified in requirements).

#### React Reviewer Application
- **Responsibility:** Provide a web interface for reviewing flagged guardrail defects with bounding-box overlays, managing review queues, and logging approval, dismissal, or recategorization decisions.
- **Interfaces:** HTTPS web interface exposed to county reviewers; data access APIs interfacing with Amazon DynamoDB.
- **Dependencies:** Amazon Cognito, Amazon DynamoDB.
- **Technology:** React (TypeScript) hosted on Amazon S3 / Amazon CloudFront (DEFAULT — not specified in requirements).

#### Amazon Cognito
- **Responsibility:** Authenticate county users and federate identity directly to the county's Active Directory using AD FS.
- **Interfaces:** OpenID Connect (OIDC) / SAML federation endpoints used by React applications and AWS API Gateway.
- **Dependencies:** County AD FS infrastructure.
- **Technology:** Amazon Cognito User Pools integrated with SAML 2.0 / AD FS.

#### Amazon S3 Raw Video Bucket
- **Responsibility:** Securely store incoming uncompressed GoPro video files and support lifecycle, versioning, and access control policies.
- **Interfaces:** S3 API REST endpoints for multipart uploads and object-created event generation.
- **Dependencies:** None.
- **Technology:** Amazon S3 with server-side encryption and S3 Versioning enabled.

#### Amazon EventBridge
- **Responsibility:** Detect object creation events in the S3 raw-video bucket and route them to start the Step Functions workflow.
- **Interfaces:** AWS EventBridge event bus rules.
- **Dependencies:** Amazon S3 Raw Video Bucket, AWS Step Functions.
- **Technology:** Amazon EventBridge.

#### AWS Step Functions Pipeline
- **Responsibility:** Orchestrate the multi-stage video processing workflow, handle explicit start/stop commands for the inference endpoint, manage distributed map parallelization, and route execution errors.
- **Interfaces:** Step Functions state machine execution APIs.
- **Dependencies:** AWS Elemental MediaConvert, AWS Fargate, Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels, Amazon DynamoDB.
- **Technology:** AWS Step Functions (Standard Workflow with Distributed Map).

#### AWS Elemental MediaConvert
- **Responsibility:** Segment and transcode long-form video files into manageable chunks following telemetry extraction.
- **Interfaces:** MediaConvert job creation and status polling APIs invoked by Step Functions.
- **Dependencies:** Amazon S3 Raw Video Bucket.
- **Technology:** AWS Elemental MediaConvert.

#### AWS Fargate Telemetry Extraction Service
- **Responsibility:** Decode the complete GPMF telemetry stream from original, unmodified video files prior to transcoding and write a normalized GPS track (JSON/Parquet) to S3.
- **Interfaces:** CLI / Container execution interface invoked by Step Functions.
- **Dependencies:** Amazon S3 Raw Video Bucket.
- **Technology:** AWS Fargate running containerized Node.js/TypeScript application code.

#### AWS Fargate Frame Processing Service
- **Responsibility:** Execute distributed map tasks to sample video frames at distance intervals (every 3 meters), run FFmpeg blur detection filtering, and correlate frames against normalized GPS tracks.
- **Interfaces:** CLI / Container execution interface invoked by Step Functions.
- **Dependencies:** Normalized GPS track in S3, transcoded video chunks.
- **Technology:** AWS Fargate running containerized Node.js/TypeScript and FFmpeg binaries.

#### Detection Service Adapter Layer
- **Responsibility:** Abstract and handle communication between frame processing tasks and the underlying computer vision model, packaging frames and parsing detection results.
- **Interfaces:** Internal programmatic function library invoked within the processing pipeline.
- **Dependencies:** Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels.
- **Technology:** TypeScript module embedded within Fargate container tasks.

#### Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels
- **Responsibility:** Execute computer vision object detection on usable frames to identify defined guardrail defect categories, returning bounding boxes, categories, and confidence scores.
- **Interfaces:** AWS SDK Rekognition Custom Labels API (`DetectCustomLabels`).
- **Dependencies:** Trained custom object detection model endpoint.
- **Technology:** Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels.

#### Detection Consolidation & Clustering Service
- **Responsibility:** Cluster raw bounding-box detections of the same physical defect across multiple nearby frames using GPS proximity, time, and category into a single representative review item.
- **Interfaces:** Internal batch processing / event handler interface.
- **Dependencies:** Amazon DynamoDB.
- **Technology:** Node.js/TypeScript service execution via AWS Lambda or Fargate (DEFAULT — not specified in requirements).

#### Amazon DynamoDB
- **Responsibility:** Store consolidated defect items, review decisions, audit trails, and review-labeled training datasets with point-in-time recovery.
- **Interfaces:** DynamoDB PartiQL / NoSQL API.
- **Dependencies:** None.
- **Technology:** Amazon DynamoDB with Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR) enabled.

#### Esri ArcGIS Integration Service
- **Responsibility:** Integrate confirmed damage findings and shared query logic with the county's existing Esri ArcGIS platform to support map dashboards, GIS layers, and export reporting.
- **Interfaces:** REST APIs and shared query data connectors.
- **Dependencies:** Amazon DynamoDB, County Esri ArcGIS platform.
- **Technology:** Node.js/TypeScript integration service interfacing with Esri ArcGIS REST API (DEFAULT — not specified in requirements).

## 5. Data Architecture

### Data Stores
| Store | Type | Technology | Purpose | Requirement Trace |
|-------|------|------------|---------|------------------|
| S3 Raw-Video Bucket | Object | Amazon S3 | Landing zone for uncompressed, long-form GoPro video uploads via presigned multipart upload. | FR-001, AC-002 |
| S3 Processed Data Bucket | Object | Amazon S3 | Storage for normalized, timestamp-indexed GPS tracks (JSON/Parquet) and geotagged, quality-filtered still frames. | FR-002, FR-003, AC-004 |
| Defect Review & Audit Database | NoSQL | Amazon DynamoDB | Storage for consolidated review items, bounding-box metadata, review audit trails (reviewer identity, timestamps, original vs. corrected labels), and training dataset references. | FR-007, AC-010, Data Requirements |

### Key Data Models
- **Video Metadata & GPS Track Model:** Tracks session-level ingestion metrics alongside timestamp-indexed GPS coordinates (JSON/Parquet format) extracted directly from original GPMF streams, establishing precise frame-to-location correlation.
- **Geotagged Frame Model:** Represents individual extracted still frames sampled at 3-meter intervals, linking image file paths in S3 to latitude, longitude, timestamp, and FFmpeg blurdetect quality metadata.
- **Consolidated Defect Item Model:** Represents a deduplicated, clustered physical defect (broken/severed, bent/deformed, missing, corroded/rusted, misaligned/leaning posts) derived from multiple nearby frames. Stores bounding-box coordinates, category labels, confidence scores, and cluster metrics.
- **Review Audit Trail Model:** Records human-in-the-loop decisions linked to consolidated defect items, capturing reviewer ID, timestamps, action taken (approve, dismiss, recategorize), priority assignment (Critical, Urgent, Moderate), and immutable tracking of original AI labels versus corrected labels.

### Data Flow
1. Data enters from field vehicles via GoPro video uploads directly to the S3 raw-video bucket using presigned multipart upload, triggered via the React web application.
2. Data is processed by the AWS Step Functions workflow and AWS Fargate tasks: original files are parsed for GPMF telemetry to generate normalized GPS tracks in S3, video chunks are segmented via AWS Elemental MediaConvert, frames are extracted at 3-meter intervals and filtered via FFmpeg blurdetect, and frames are evaluated by Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels.
3. Data is stored in Amazon S3 (raw videos, GPS tracks, geotagged frames) and Amazon DynamoDB (consolidated defect items, review queues, audit trails, and future training datasets).
4. Data is served to county inspectors and reviewers through the React reviewer application for queue management and audit updates, and exported/queried via shared query logic to the Esri ArcGIS map dashboard and reporting engines for CSV, PDF, and GeoJSON outputs.

### Data Ownership & Governance
| Data Domain | Owner | Classification | Retention |
|-------------|-------|---------------|-----------|
| Raw Video & Processed Frames | County Video-Based Guardrail Inspection Program | Internal | Standard S3 access controls with lifecycle and retention policies; S3 versioning enabled. |
| Telemetry & GPS Tracks | Pipeline (Telemetry Extraction Service on AWS Fargate) | Internal | Retained alongside processed video artifacts in S3. |
| Review Queue & Audit Trails | County Inspectors / Reviewers | Internal | Retained in Amazon DynamoDB with point-in-time recovery enabled; review-labeled datasets retained for future model retraining. |

---

#### ADR-DATA-001: Selection of Amazon DynamoDB for Defect Queues and Audit Trails
- **Status:** Approved
- **Context:** The system requires a high-availability, low-latency datastore to manage consolidated defect review items, bounding-box metadata, human review decisions, and immutable audit trails that feed both operational workflows and future model retraining pipelines.
- **Decision:** Use Amazon DynamoDB as the primary transactional and operational data store for review items and audit trails.
- **Consequences:** Provides seamless serverless scalability, sub-millisecond query performance for the React reviewer application, and built-in point-in-time recovery supporting compliance and audit retention requirements.
- **Requirement Trace:** FR-007, AC-010, 7.3 Availability, Data Requirements.

sections.content:
## 6. Integration Architecture

### APIs
| Endpoint | Method | Purpose | Auth | Requirement Trace |
|----------|--------|---------|------|------------------|
| `/upload/presign` | POST | Generates an Amazon S3 presigned multipart upload URL for direct-to-S3 video ingestion | Amazon Cognito (JWT Bearer Token via AD FS federation) | FR-001 |
| `/defects` | GET | Retrieves paginated and filtered lists of consolidated defect items for the React reviewer application | Amazon Cognito (JWT Bearer Token via AD FS federation) | FR-007 |
| `/defects/{id}` | PATCH | Updates defect review status (approve, dismiss, recategorize) and records audit trail entries | Amazon Cognito (JWT Bearer Token via AD FS federation) | FR-007 |
| `/reports` | GET | Exports inspection reports and summaries in CSV, PDF, or GeoJSON formats | Amazon Cognito (JWT Bearer Token via AD FS federation) | FR-008 |
| `/gis/query` | GET | Shared query logic endpoint providing spatial and attribute data for the Esri ArcGIS map dashboard | Amazon Cognito (JWT Bearer Token via AD FS federation) | FR-008 |

### Message Queues / Event Bus
| Topic/Queue | Producer | Consumer | Pattern | Purpose |
|-------------|----------|----------|---------|---------|
| `s3-object-created-raw-video` | Amazon S3 (Raw Video Bucket) | Amazon EventBridge | Pub-Sub | Automatically triggers the AWS Step Functions workflow upon video upload completion | FR-003, AC-003 |
| `processing-dlq` | AWS Step Functions / AWS Fargate | Dead-Letter Queue (Amazon SQS) | Queue | Captures unhandled failures from video segmentation, telemetry extraction, and damage detection for operational review | AI Requirements (Fallback) |

### Third-Party Integrations
| Service | Purpose | Protocol | SLA |
|---------|---------|----------|-----|
| County Active Directory Federation Services (AD FS) | Enterprise user authentication via SAML/OIDC federation | HTTPS / SAML 2.0 / OIDC | DEFAULT — not specified in requirements. (Recommended default: 99.9% availability matching corporate identity standards). |
| Esri ArcGIS Platform | Geospatial map dashboard visualization and spatial reporting integration | REST API / ArcGIS SDK | DEFAULT — not specified in requirements. (Recommended default: 99.9% availability matching county GIS infrastructure). |

### Authentication & Authorization Flows
1. **Login:** A county user accesses the React web application and initiates login. The application redirects the user to Amazon Cognito, which federates the authentication request directly to the county's Active Directory via AD FS (Active Directory Federation Services).
2. **Token Issuance:** Upon successful validation against county Active Directory credentials, AD FS returns assertions to Amazon Cognito, which issues a secure JSON Web Token (JWT) back to the React application.
3. **Token Validation:** API requests originating from the React application include the JWT bearer token in the `Authorization` header. Backend API handlers (or API Gateway authorizers) validate the JWT signature, expiration, and claims.
4. **Authorization:** Authorized users access direct backend services (such as presigned upload generation, review queues, and report exports). For video uploads, authenticated users obtain Amazon S3 presigned multipart upload URLs to transfer files directly to the S3 Raw Zone, bypassing API payload limitations.

---

### Architecture Decision Records (ADRs)

#### ADR-001: Direct-to-S3 Presigned Multipart Uploads for Video Ingestion
- **Status:** Approved
- **Context:** Long-form GoPro video files are 1–2 hours in duration and substantial in file size. Routing such payloads through API Gateway and backend compute services would violate payload limits and consume excessive network bandwidth.
- **Decision:** Use Amazon Cognito authenticated React frontend to request an S3 presigned multipart upload URL and upload video files directly to the Amazon S3 raw-video bucket.
- **Consequences:** Eliminates API Gateway payload size bottlenecks and reduces backend compute overhead during ingestion, fulfilling FR-001 and AC-002.

#### ADR-002: Amazon EventBridge for S3-Triggered Workflow Orchestration
- **Status:** Approved
- **Context:** Video uploads to Amazon S3 need to reliably kick off the automated computer vision processing pipeline without tightly coupling storage events to compute logic.
- **Decision:** Route Amazon S3 object-created events through Amazon EventBridge to explicitly trigger the AWS Step Functions workflow.
- **Consequences:** Provides a decoupled, filterable, and event-driven architecture that scales reliably, satisfying FR-003 and AC-003.

#### ADR-003: Token-Based Authentication via Amazon Cognito and AD FS Federation
- **Status:** Approved
- **Context:** County users must authenticate using existing enterprise credentials without requiring a separate credential store.
- **Decision:** Configure Amazon Cognito to federate authentication directly with the county's AD FS (Active Directory Federation Services) and issue JWT tokens for API authorization.
- **Consequences:** Centralizes identity management within county Active Directory, securing the React application and downstream APIs in compliance with FR-001 and AC-001.

## 8. Security Architecture

### Authentication
- **Mechanism:** OAuth 2.0 / SAML 2.0 Federation via Active Directory Federation Services (AD FS) (Traceability: REQ-001, FR-001, AC-001)
- **Provider:** Amazon Cognito User Pools federated to county AD FS (Traceability: REQ-001, FR-001, AC-001)
- **Token Strategy:** JSON Web Tokens (JWT) issued by Amazon Cognito for session management across the React web applications

### Authorization
- **Model:** Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) (Traceability: REQ-001, FR-007)
- **Roles:** 
  - `County Inspector / Reviewer`: Access to the React Reviewer application, ability to review flagged items, approve, dismiss, recategorize defects, assign priorities, and export inspection reports (Traceability: REQ-001, FR-007, FR-008)
  - `County Administrator / Uploader`: Access to the React Upload application for uploading raw video footage, plus administrative oversight (Traceability: REQ-001, FR-001)

### Data Encryption
- **At Rest:** AES-256 encryption applied to all stored data, including Amazon S3 buckets (Raw Zone, frame stores) and Amazon DynamoDB tables containing audit trails and review items (Traceability: REQ-001, Section 7.3 NFRs)
- **In Transit:** TLS 1.3 enforced for all data transmitted between the React front-end clients, API endpoints, S3 presigned multipart uploads, and AWS internal service communications
- **Key Management:** AWS Key Management Service (KMS) using customer-managed keys (CMKs) for S3 and DynamoDB encryption control

### Network Security
- **Firewall:** DEFAULT — no network security requirements specified in REQ-001. Recommend adding network security requirements before finalizing architecture. *Sensible default:* AWS WAF (Web Application Firewall) attached to Amazon CloudFront / API Gateway distributing the React application; Amazon VPC security groups isolating AWS Fargate processing tasks within private subnets.
- **DDoS Protection:** DEFAULT — no network security requirements specified in REQ-001. Recommend adding network security requirements before finalizing architecture. *Sensible default:* AWS Shield Standard enabled automatically on all AWS public endpoints.

### Compliance Mapping

| DEFAULT — no regulatory compliance requirements specified in REQ-001 | Recommend conducting a formal data privacy and legal review regarding public road video capture. | Gap |

## 8. Security Architecture

### Authentication
- **Mechanism:** OAuth 2.0 / SAML 2.0 Federation via Active Directory Federation Services (AD FS) (Traceability: REQ-001, FR-001, AC-001)
- **Provider:** Amazon Cognito User Pools federated to county AD FS (Traceability: REQ-001, FR-001, AC-001)
- **Token Strategy:** JSON Web Tokens (JWT) issued by Amazon Cognito for session management across the React web applications

### Authorization
- **Model:** Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) (Traceability: REQ-001, FR-007)
- **Roles:** 
  - `County Inspector / Reviewer`: Access to the React Reviewer application, ability to review flagged items, approve, dismiss, recategorize defects, assign priorities, and export inspection reports (Traceability: REQ-001, FR-007, FR-008)
  - `County Administrator / Uploader`: Access to the React Upload application for uploading raw video footage, plus administrative oversight (Traceability: REQ-001, FR-001)

### Data Encryption
- **At Rest:** AES-256 encryption applied to all stored data, including Amazon S3 buckets (Raw Zone, frame stores) and Amazon DynamoDB tables containing audit trails and review items (Traceability: REQ-001, Section 7.3 NFRs)
- **In Transit:** TLS 1.3 enforced for all data transmitted between the React front-end clients, API endpoints, S3 presigned multipart uploads, and AWS internal service communications
- **Key Management:** AWS Key Management Service (KMS) using customer-managed keys (CMKs) for S3 and DynamoDB encryption control

### Network Security
- **Firewall:** DEFAULT — no network security requirements specified in REQ-001. Recommend adding network security requirements before finalizing architecture. *Sensible default:* AWS WAF (Web Application Firewall) attached to Amazon CloudFront / API Gateway distributing the React application; Amazon VPC security groups isolating AWS Fargate processing tasks within private subnets.
- **DDoS Protection:** DEFAULT — no network security requirements specified in REQ-001. Recommend adding network security requirements before finalizing architecture. *Sensible default:* AWS Shield Standard enabled automatically on all AWS public endpoints.

### Compliance Mapping
| Compliance Requirement | Architecture Control | Status |
|-----------------------|---------------------|--------|
| Standard S3 access controls for data retention regarding incidental faces or license plates captured on public roads (internal tool only) (Traceability: REQ-001, Section 7.5) | Restricted S3 bucket policies, private-only access via IAM roles, and exclusion of public exposure for raw video and processed frames. | Addressed |
| Complete audit trail of every review decision including reviewer identity, timestamp, original AI label, and corrected label (Traceability: REQ-001, FR-007, AC-010) | Immutable audit log records written to Amazon DynamoDB with point-in-time recovery enabled. | Addressed |
| DEFAULT — no regulatory compliance requirements specified in REQ-001 | Recommend conducting a formal data privacy and legal review regarding public road video capture. | Gap |

### Secret Management
- **Tool:** AWS Secrets Manager / Parameter Store (Traceability: REQ-001, Section 5 architecture pattern)
- **Rotation Policy:** DEFAULT — no secret rotation requirements specified in REQ-001. Recommend adding rotation policies before finalizing architecture. *Sensible default:* Automatic quarterly rotation for database credentials, API keys, and service integration tokens.

### Performance
| NFR | Architecture Approach | Target | Measurement |
|-----|----------------------|--------|-------------|
| DEFAULT — NFRs not specified in REQ-001. Frame extraction, quality filtering, and object detection processing latency. | AWS Step Functions (Distributed Map) combined with AWS Fargate parallel task execution to process chunks concurrently. | Process a 1-hour video file within 30 minutes. | CloudWatch metrics tracking total workflow execution duration from S3 upload completion to final DynamoDB cluster write. |
| DEFAULT — NFRs not specified in REQ-001. React reviewer application and map dashboard UI responsiveness. | React web application served via Amazon S3 / Amazon CloudFront CDN with API requests routed through Amazon API Gateway. | Page load time < 2 seconds; API response time < 500ms. | Real User Monitoring (RUM) / CloudWatch synthesized monitoring and client-side performance tracing. |

### Scalability
- **Approach:** Horizontal / Auto-scaling
- **Strategy:** Long-form video processing scales horizontally via AWS Step Functions Distributed Map, dynamically spawning AWS Fargate tasks to process video chunks and extract 3-meter interval frames in parallel. Compute resources scale elastically based on workload size without hitting single-function execution limits (REQ-003, REQ-004, FR-003, FR-004). Database scalability is handled by Amazon DynamoDB on-demand capacity mode, automatically scaling read and write throughput to match review queue and audit trail activity (REQ-007, FR-007).

### Availability & Resilience
- **Target SLA:** DEFAULT — not specified in REQ-001. Target standard enterprise availability of 99.9% for core review and data storage services.
- **Redundancy:** Multi-AZ deployment across AWS managed services (Amazon S3, DynamoDB, Fargate, Step Functions, Cognito, and API Gateway).
- **Failover:** Automatic Multi-AZ failover managed natively by AWS foundational services. Failed frame extraction or detection tasks are routed to a Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ) to ensure system resilience and prevent silent pipeline failures (REQ-005, AI Requirements).
- **Disaster Recovery:** RPO: Near-zero (continuous point-in-time recovery enabled on Amazon DynamoDB). RTO: < 4 hours via automated infrastructure-as-code deployment and S3 bucket versioning/backups (REQ-003, REQ-007, Data Retention).

### Monitoring & Observability
| Signal | Tool | Purpose |
|--------|------|---------|
| Logs | Amazon CloudWatch Logs | Capture execution logs from AWS Fargate tasks, Step Functions workflow transitions, and API requests. |
| Metrics | Amazon CloudWatch Metrics | Monitor resource utilization, Fargate task execution counts, Step Functions success/failure rates, DynamoDB throttling, and Rekognition Custom Labels endpoint activation status. |
| Traces | AWS X-Ray | End-to-end distributed tracing across API Gateway, Step Functions, Fargate tasks, and downstream AWS services. |
| Alerts | Amazon CloudWatch Alarms & Amazon SNS | Trigger notifications for pipeline failures, Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ) message accumulation, and inference endpoint start/stop anomalies (R-003). |

sections.title: Risks & Mitigations
sections.content:
## 11. Architecture Risks & Mitigations

### Technical Risks
| # | Risk | Probability | Impact | Mitigation | Owner |
|---|------|------------|--------|------------|-------|
| AR-001 | High labeling effort required for bounding-box object detection compared to image classification (Source: R-001) | Medium | High | Sourced and scoped as part of the initial labeling effort and dataset sizing (targeting several hundred labeled images per defect class) (Source: R-001). | DEFAULT — not specified in requirements (Assigned owner: Information not available — requires clarification from [Business Owner / Technical Lead / Stakeholder]) |
| AR-002 | Potential schedule slip due to delays in county IT/GIS decisions regarding Active Directory federation (AD FS) and Esri ArcGIS integration (Source: R-002, Dependencies) | High | High | Address open decisions and coordination dependencies during the Discover + Design phase with county IT and GIS teams (Source: R-002). | DEFAULT — not specified in requirements (Assigned owner: Information not available — requires clarification from [Business Owner / Technical Lead / Stakeholder]) |
| AR-003 | High AWS Rekognition Custom Labels running costs if start/stop logic fails in Step Functions (Source: R-003) | Medium | High | Explicitly start and stop the inference endpoint within the Step Functions workflow before and after the damage detection stage (Source: R-003, AC-008). | DEFAULT — not specified in requirements (Assigned owner: Information not available — requires clarification from [Business Owner / Technical Lead / Stakeholder]) |
| AR-004 | Privacy and compliance risks associated with capturing faces and license plates on public roads (Source: R-004) | Low | Medium | Mitigated by standard S3 access controls, which are sufficient for data retention and privacy regarding incidental faces/plates since this is an internal tool (Source: R-004, NFR 7.5 Compliance). | DEFAULT — not specified in requirements (Assigned owner: Information not available — requires clarification from [Business Owner / Technical Lead / Stakeholder]) |
| AR-005 | Visually similar defect categories causing low model precision (Source: R-005) | Medium | Medium | Train with several hundred labeled images per class and merge categories if precision is low; utilize a fixed golden/regression test set and versioned confidence thresholds (Source: R-005, AI Requirements). | DEFAULT — not specified in requirements (Assigned owner: Information not available — requires clarification from [Business Owner / Technical Lead / Stakeholder]) |

### Architecture Debt & Trade-offs
| Trade-off | Chosen Approach | Alternative | Rationale |
|-----------|----------------|-------------|-----------|
| Distance-based frame sampling vs. fixed frame-rate sampling (Source: FR-003) | Sample frames at fixed distance intervals (every 3 meters) using GPS telemetry parsed via AWS Fargate (Source: FR-003, AC-005). | Sample frames at fixed time intervals (e.g., every 1 second) regardless of vehicle speed. | Distance-based sampling optimizes S3 storage and Rekognition inference costs by processing consistent physical increments regardless of vehicle speed fluctuations (Source: Section 5 Key Changes). |
| Pre-transcoding GPMF telemetry extraction vs. post-transcoding metadata parsing (Source: FR-002) | Decode the complete GPMF telemetry stream directly from the original, unmodified video file prior to segmentation or transcoding (Source: FR-002, AC-004). | Extract telemetry tracks concurrently with or after AWS Elemental MediaConvert video chunking. | Ensures frame-to-location correlation is protected and reliable before video files are split or transcoded (Source: FR-002 User Story). |
| Explicit Step Functions inference endpoint lifecycle management vs. always-on Rekognition endpoint (Source: AC-008) | Explicitly start the Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels inference endpoint before the detection stage and stop it immediately afterward via Step Functions (Source: AC-008). | Maintain a continuously running, always-on dedicated inference endpoint. | Prevents high idle billing costs for custom labels endpoints during periods when video ingestion and processing pipelines are inactive (Source: R-003). |

### Assumptions
| # | Assumption | Impact if Wrong |
|---|-----------|----------------|
| AA-001 | The county's GoPro cameras reliably capture high-quality GPMF telemetry streams, because the architecture depends on parsing embedded metadata without video corruption (Source: A-001). | The telemetry extraction service will fail or produce invalid GPS tracks, breaking the frame-to-location correlation pipeline (Source: A-001). |
| AA-002 | A single-stack Node.js/TypeScript architecture is acceptable to the county's IT department, because the provided architecture heavily specifies TypeScript across frontend, backend, Fargate, and CDK (Source: A-002). | The county may require a different technology stack (such as Python), requiring architectural rework or team retraining (Source: A-002). |
| AA-003 | A team of approximately 3 engineers will execute the project, based on the effort estimation guidelines provided in the technical documents (Source: A-003). | Resource allocation may be insufficient, leading to schedule delays or project delivery slippage (Source: A-003). |

sections.title: Architecture Decision Records
sections.content:
## 12. Architecture Decision Records (ADRs)

### ADR-001: Use Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels via Adapter Layer for Guardrail Defect Detection
- **Status:** Proposed
- **Context:** The system must automatically detect specific roadside guardrail defects (broken/severed, bent/deformed, missing, corroded/rusted, and misaligned/leaning posts) with bounding boxes and categorical labels to reduce manual review hours (REQ-001, FR-005, AC-007).
- **Decision:** Use Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels object detection model accessed via a dedicated Detection Service adapter layer, with Step Functions explicitly starting and stopping the inference endpoint per execution run.
- **Consequences:** 
  - *Positive:* Accelerates delivery by leveraging a managed AWS AI service without requiring custom MLOps infrastructure; explicit start/stop lifecycle management directly controls inference costs (R-003).
  - *Negative:* Bound by Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels pricing and service limits; requires maintaining an adapter layer to decouple business logic from the underlying vendor API.

### ADR-002: Direct-to-S3 Presigned Multipart Uploads for Long-Form Video Ingestion
- **Status:** Proposed
- **Context:** County users need to upload long-form GoPro video files (1-2 hours) containing embedded GPMF telemetry into the system securely (REQ-001, FR-001, AC-002).
- **Decision:** Implement a React web application utilizing Amazon Cognito federated to AD FS (FR-001) that generates presigned multipart upload URLs to route large video files directly into the Amazon S3 raw-video bucket.
- **Consequences:** 
  - *Positive:* Completely bypasses API Gateway and Lambda payload size/timeout limits, enabling reliable ingestion of massive video files.
  - *Negative:* Client-side implementation complexity for managing multipart chunking and retry logic in the browser.

### ADR-003: Step Functions Distributed Map with AWS Fargate for Telemetry Extraction and Frame Sampling
- **Status:** Proposed
- **Context:** Long-form video files must be processed to extract embedded GPMF telemetry prior to transcoding, and frames must be sampled at precise distance intervals (every 3 meters) while filtering out blurry frames (REQ-001, FR-002, FR-003, FR-004, AC-004, AC-005, AC-006).
- **Decision:** Use AWS Step Functions (Distributed Map) orchestrating AWS Fargate tasks to extract GPMF telemetry to a normalized JSON/Parquet track in S3, segment video chunks via AWS Elemental MediaConvert, and execute distance-based sampling with FFmpeg blur filtering.
- **Consequences:** 
  - *Positive:* Provides high scalability and parallel execution to process 1-2 hour videos reliably without hitting single-function execution limits (7.4); decouples heavy compute steps into elastic container workloads.
  - *Negative:* Increased orchestration complexity compared to monolithic processing; requires careful monitoring of Step Functions execution costs and Fargate task allocations.

### ADR-004: Amazon DynamoDB for Consolidated Defect Queue and Review Audit Trail
- **Status:** Proposed
- **Context:** Raw detections across multiple frames must be clustered into single review items, and human reviewer actions (approvals, dismissals, recategorizations) must be permanently audited with timestamps and identities (REQ-001, FR-006, FR-007, AC-009, AC-010).
- **Decision:** Use Amazon DynamoDB as the single data store for consolidated defect review items, audit trails, and downstream model retraining datasets, configured with point-in-time recovery (7.3, Data Retention).
- **Consequences:** 
  - *Positive:* Delivers single-digit millisecond latency for the React reviewer application query patterns; built-in point-in-time recovery satisfies data resilience requirements.
  - *Negative:* Query flexibility is constrained by primary key design; complex relational queries require careful table design or secondary indexes.

### ADR-005: Integration with Existing Esri ArcGIS Platform for Map Visualization and Reporting
- **Status:** Proposed
- **Context:** Confirmed damage findings and location data must be displayed on a map dashboard and exported into road/priority summaries, CSV exports, and PDF reports (REQ-001, FR-008, AC-011, AC-012).
- **Decision:** Integrate the system's spatial data outputs directly with the county's existing Esri ArcGIS platform utilizing shared query logic for map dashboards, CSV exports, and printable/PDF reports.
- **Consequences:** 
  - *Positive:* Aligns with county stakeholders' existing GIS toolsets and workflows without forcing adoption of a separate mapping solution.
  - *Negative:* Creates a dependency on external county GIS licensing, IT coordination, and schema compatibility (Dependencies).

- **Decision:** Use AWS Step Functions (Distributed Map) orchestrating AWS Fargate tasks to extract GPMF telemetry to a normalized JSON/Parquet track in S3, segment video chunks via AWS Elemental MediaConvert, and execute distance-based sampling with FFmpeg blur filtering.
- **Consequences:** 
  - *Positive:* Provides high scalability and parallel execution to process 1-2 hour videos reliably without hitting single-function execution limits (7.4); decouples heavy compute steps into elastic container workloads.
  - *Negative:* Increased orchestration complexity compared to monolithic processing; requires careful monitoring of Step Functions execution costs and Fargate task allocations.

### ADR-004: Amazon DynamoDB for Consolidated Defect Queue and Review Audit Trail
- **Status:** Proposed
- **Context:** Raw detections across multiple frames must be clustered into single review items, and human reviewer actions (approvals, dismissals, recategorizations) must be permanently audited with timestamps and identities (REQ-001, FR-006, FR-007, AC-009, AC-010).
- **Decision:** Use Amazon DynamoDB as the single data store for consolidated defect review items, audit trails, and downstream model retraining datasets, configured with point-in-time recovery (7.3, Data Retention).
- **Consequences:** 
  - *Positive:* Delivers single-digit millisecond latency for the React reviewer application query patterns; built-in point-in-time recovery satisfies data resilience requirements.
  - *Negative:* Query flexibility is constrained by primary key design; complex relational queries require careful table design or secondary indexes.

### ADR-005: Integration with Existing Esri ArcGIS Platform for Map Visualization and Reporting
- **Status:** Proposed
- **Context:** Confirmed damage findings and location data must be displayed on a map dashboard and exported into road/priority summaries, CSV exports, and PDF reports (REQ-001, FR-008, AC-011, AC-012).
- **Decision:** Integrate the system's spatial data outputs directly with the county's existing Esri ArcGIS platform utilizing shared query logic for map dashboards, CSV exports, and printable/PDF reports.
- **Consequences:** 
  - *Positive:* Aligns with county stakeholders' existing GIS toolsets and workflows without forcing adoption of a separate mapping solution.
  - *Negative:* Creates a dependency on external county GIS licensing, IT coordination, and schema compatibility (Dependencies).
